lawyer:
Md Nurul Amin Senior Advocate, instructed by Zainul Abedin Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner.

Sasti Sarker Advocate, instructed by Madhumalati Chowdhury Barua Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondent No.1.

None Represented—For the Respondent Nos.2-17.
parties:
Mosharaf Hossain (Md) ----- Petitioner
VS
Rekha Khatun and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal are that respondent No.1 as the pre-emptor instituted Miscellaneous Case No.7 of 2007 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia against the petitioner along with others for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The pre-emptor contended, inter alia, that the land measuring 0.16 acre of plot No.300 appertaining to RS Khatian No.11 under Mouza-Sultanpur belonged to Ayen Uddin, Koyaz Ali, Riaz Uddin and Torap Ali in equal share. The pre-emptor, predecessor of respondent Nos.2-7 purchased the land from Aynuddin and Koyaz Ali. After death of Riazuddin, the pre-emptor and respondent Nos.2-7 got the land as heirs and respondent Nos.8-16 got the land as heirs of Torap Ali, respondent Nos.1-8 sold out the land measuring 0.1484 acre in favour of respondent No.1 on 30-10-2006 by registered sale deed No.3531 without informing the pre-emptor. Respondent No.1 is a stranger purchaser. The pre-emptor is a co-sharer of the jama. So, the pre-emptor is entitled to get the said land by way of pre-emption, hence she filed the instant Case. 

 3. The learned Assistant Judge by order dated 25-2-2007 directed the pre-emptor to deposit remaining 15% Court fee as well as interest at the rate of 8% as per the amended provision of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. On 13-3-2007 the pre-emptor deposited remaining 15% of the sale price as well as 8% interest amounting to Taka 7,929 and the learned Assistant Judge ordered to accept the Challan. 

 4. Thereafter pre-emptee No.1 on 20-10-2009 by filling an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure prayed for dismissal of the case on the ground that the deposit has not been made as per the amended provision of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as deposit of 10% towards compensation money is not valid deposit and, as such, the case is barred under 96(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 7. Mr Md Nurul Amin, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was amended by Act No. XXXIV of 2006 wherein section 96(3)(b)(c) provides that an application under sub-section (1) shall be dismissed unless the applicant or applicants, at the time of making it, deposit in the Court compensation at the rate of twenty five per centum of the amount referred to in clause (a) and an amount calculated at the rate of eight per centum simple annual interest upon the amount referred to in clause (a) for the period from the date of the execution of the deed of sale to the date of filling of the application for pre-emption. But the pre-emptor did not deposit 25% of compensation along with 8% interest. In view of the fact the lower revisional Court correctly rejected the plaint, but the High Court Division misinterpreted the amended language and made the Rule absolute which occasioned failure of justice and, as such, the judgment of the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. He further submitted that the trial Court had no jurisdiction to allow the pre-emptor to deposit the shortfall amount of the compensation. But on 25-2-2007 the trial Court allowed the pre-emptor to deposit the shortfall amount which is totally illegal and, as such, it is not necessary to challenge the order dated 25-2-2007. The High' Court Division erred in law in holding that since the pre-emptor did not challenge the said order, so it remained immune from challenge. He submitted that though the pre-emptor deposited Taka 7,929 on 13-3-2007 in spite of that the pre-emptordid not deposit the full amount according to amended section 96(3)(b)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and, as such, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute. He submitted that the notice was not served upon the pre-emptee and subsequently notice was served under Order V, rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereafter he filed an application for rejection of plaint under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, so the finding of the High Court Division that the pre-emptee filed the application for rejection of plaint by ill intention is erroneous and unwarranted. He submitted that the only point in issue is whether the pre-emption case is barred by any law and in this case, it is crystal clear that the pre-emptor did not deposit the compensation with interest, so the pre-emption case is barred by law. But the High Court Division erroneously made the Rule absolute by making out a third case which is totally unwarranted and, as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. In support of his contention, he referred to the decision in the case of Md Ruhul Amin being dead his heirs Ayesha Amin and others vs Mohammad Forkan. Ullah and another 2017(2) LNJ (AD) 130 = 70 DLR (AD) 123 wherein one of us was party. 

 10. We note at the outset that the pre-emption case was filed on 16-1-2007 4(four) months after the amendment of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Any application filed even one day after the coming into force of any law must be in accordance with the law which exists on the date of filing. 

 "96(3)(a) An application made under sub-section (1) shall be dismissed unless the applicant or applicants, at the time of making it, deposit in the Court the amount of the consideration money or the value of the transferred holding or portion or share of the holding as stated in the notice under section 89 or in the deed of transfer, as the case may be, together with compensation at the rate of ten per centum of such amount. 

 (b) On receipt of such application accompanied by such deposit, the Court shall give notice to the transferee and to the other persons made parties thereto under sub-section (2) to appear within such period as it may fix and shall require such persons to state the consideration money actually paid for the transfer and shall also require the transferee to state what other sums he has paid in respect of rent since the date of transfer and what expenses he has incurred in annulling encumbrances on, or for making any improvement in respect of, the holding, portion or share transferred, and the Court shall then, after giving all the parties an opportunity of being heard after holding an enquiry as to the actual amounts of the consideration money and rent paid and the expenses incurred by the transferee in annulling encumbrances on, or for the improvement of, the land transferred, direct the applicant or applicants to deposit a further sum, if necessary, within such period as it thinks reasonable: 

 (a) the amount of the consideration money of the sold holding or portion or share of the holding as stated in the notice under section 89 or in the deed of sale, as the case may be; 

 13. Since the amendment, sections 96(4) and 96(5) have also become relevant in the context of deposits made in Court. Section 96(4) and 96(5) provide as follows: "96(4) On receipt of such application accompanied by such deposits, the Court shall give notice to the purchaser and to the other persons made parties thereto under sub-section (2) to appear within such period as it may fix and shall require the purchaser to state what other sums he has paid in respect of rent since the date of sale and what expenses he has incurred in annulling encumbrances on, or for making any improvement in respect of the holding, portion or share sold. 

 15. Hence, there was power given to the Court to hold an inquiry regarding actual amounts of consideration money etc. and to allow further amounts to be deposited within a certain period after filing the application. After the amendment of the law there is no such power given to the Court to hold any inquiry regarding consideration money or allow time or opportunity to deposit in Court any amount in respect of shortfall of consideration, compensation and interest. The present sub-section (4) of section 96 provides that "the Court shall give notice to the purchaser and to the other persons made parties thereto...and shall require the purchaser to state what other sums he has paid in respect of rent since the date of sale and what expenses he has incurred in annulling encumbrances on or making any improvement..." 

 Accordingly, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is set-aside and the order of the District Judge, Kushtia dated 29-2-2012 is hereby upheld and the application filed by the pre-emptee under Order VII, rule 11 is allowed. The application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption is rejected.
